$comment: Cursor's docs now present `agent` as the primary command, but the installer still ships `cursor-agent` and `agent` is far too generic a name to probe for (`command -v agent` can false-positive on unrelated binaries). `cursor-agent` remains supported as the stable alias, so it is both the probe target and the launch binary.

auto.$comment: Cursor's own auto mode, and mechanically the closest analogue to Claude Code's anywhere in this set. `cursor-agent --help`: `--auto-review  Use Auto-review (Smart Auto): a server classifier auto-runs safe tool calls and prompts for the rest`. A classifier decides, not a sandbox — so this belongs on the same rung as Claude Code's auto rather than beside Codex's workspace-write.
auto.label: Auto — a classifier runs the safe calls, prompts for the rest

bypass.$comment: `--yolo` is documented as an alias for `--force`; only one is sent.
bypass.label: Bypass all approvals (dangerous)

modelSelection.$comment: Cursor's model roster is subscription-entitlement-dependent and churns often, so no ids are seeded — the user adds the models their plan actually has via Settings (the no-guess policy from BUNDLED_AGENT_MODEL_CATALOGS applies to the manifest seed here too).

resume.$comment: Cursor documents `--resume <chat-id>` and `--continue` (previous session). Mirrors the OpenCode wiring: --continue as the base, the explicit resume pair only when the caller has an id. Unverified end-to-end, so capabilities.resumeSession stays false until confirmed against a real install (MC-1464/MC-1465 discipline).

contextInjection.$comment: cursor-agent documents no system-prompt flag, no rules flag and no instructions env var (verified against the installed CLI: --help lists --model / --mode / --add-dir / --plugin-dir and nothing that sets a system prompt). Its only out-of-band channel is a rules FILE inside the user's repo, which the host must not write into. So the document is wrapped in <host-context> tags and placed BEFORE the user's prompt.

mcpConfig.$comment: Cursor reads workspace MCP servers from .cursor/mcp.json in the same {"mcpServers": {...}} shape Claude Code uses, so the claude-code writer applies as-is.

agentStateSpec.$comment: Cursor's CLI ships lifecycle hooks (2026-01-16 CLI update): project-level .cursor/hooks.json in the flat {version, hooks: {<event>: [{command}]}} shape, camelCase event names, snake_case stdin payload with hook_event_name/conversation_id/transcript_path base fields (conversation_id is the resume chat id; the shared reporter forwards it as the session id). awaiting_input is DELIBERATELY unsupported: Cursor has no Notification/PermissionRequest-style event — its permission flow consults beforeShellExecution/beforeMCPExecution hooks, which fire on every tool run and whose empty-stdout response semantics are unverified, so registering a reporter there risks interfering with approvals rather than observing them. Until verified against a real install (rides kimi-cursor-e2e-verification), a Cursor permission prompt reads as its last working phase and the stall watchdog is the backstop. stop's payload carries status completed|aborted|error — all three end the turn (idle+turnEnd), and error/aborted additionally flag the turn FAILED via failureWhen, so an automation run whose Cursor turn crashes or is interrupted finalizes as failed instead of opening a PR from unfinished work.

capabilities.$comment: resumeSession is intentionally false pending end-to-end verification (MC-1464/MC-1465 discipline); the resume argv above is wired for the flip. sessionIdFromCaller is false because Cursor mints its own chat ids (no --session-id-style launch assignment is documented).
